vulnerable_statements.reason: intsize is read from the device tree's "#interrupt-cells" property and is never checked against MAX_PHANDLE_ARGS, the fixed size of out_irq->args. If a device tree sets a large #interrupt-cells value, the loop runs past the end of the array.
Writes to out_irq->args + i for every i < intsize. When intsize > MAX_PHANDLE_ARGS, this writes past the end of the fixed-size args[] array (stack or heap out-of-bounds write).

The length of the "reg" property is thrown away, and the raw pointer goes to of_irq_parse_raw. That function may read #address-cells words from it, which can be more than the property actually holds (out-of-bounds read).

suggested_fix: After reading #interrupt-cells, reject values larger than MAX_PHANDLE_ARGS, e.g. if (WARN_ON(intsize > MAX_PHANDLE_ARGS)) { res = -EINVAL; goto out; }, before setting args_count and copying. For the reg property, get its length with of_get_property(device, "reg", &len). Copy at most min(len, sizeof(addr_buf)) bytes into a zero-initialized local buffer of MAX_PHANDLE_ARGS cells, and pass that buffer to of_irq_parse_raw instead of the raw property pointer.
